findings.finding: Since the July 2024 divestiture of the Russian businesses (above 95% of then revenue) NBIS is a new company: an AI-specialised GPU cloud (Nebius AI cloud 574.9M of 582.3M Q2 2026 revenue, 98.7%) that sells capacity under multi-year take-or-pay contracts and on demand. FY2020-FY2023 companyfacts revenue (2.96-8.92B) is the old Yandex group and is not this business's history.

Growth is structural capacity growth, not cyclical or macro: AI cloud revenue 93.7M -> 574.9M (Q2 2025 -> Q2 2026, about 6.1x) as connected power rose from about 170 MW (end 2025) toward the 800-1,000 MW year-end 2026 guide; ARR 1.9B (March) -> 3.0B (June) -> guided 7-9B at year end. The residual mix effect is minor (Avride 1.0M, TripleTen 10.0M and shrinking 19% y/y).

Demand is contracted: RPO 37.49B at 2026-06-30 (36% within 24 months, 40% in months 25-48), management backlog above 40B including investment-grade long-term deals (Microsoft up to about 17.4B through 2031; Meta about 12B over five years from early 2027). Customers prepay: deferred revenue 5.98B, over 9B prepayments expected in 2026, upfront payments about 55% of associated capex on the Q2 landmark deals. Firm exposure is concentrated: three unnamed customers were 24%, 21% and 14% of Q2 2026 revenue (59%); prepayments are partly refundable and contracts carry service credits and tranche termination on delivery delays.

Q2 landmark deals price at 20-25M USD of annual contract value per MW (about 22.5M midpoint); Nebius AI cloud adjusted EBITDA margin 50% in Q2 2026 (285.7M), group about 41%. But D&A was 259.7M (44.6% of revenue) in Q2 because capacity is installed before revenue, so GAAP operating margin was -30.2%; server useful life was extended from 4 to 5 years in 2026, which flatters depreciation.

Capex 8.13B in H1 2026 (5.66B in Q2) against operating cash flow 4.50B that is itself mostly customer prepayments (deferred revenue +4.40B); 2026 capex guide 20-25B. H1 funding: 4.34B convertibles, 2.85B treasury share sales (ATM), 2.0B NVIDIA pre-funded warrants; then a 4.5B convertible offering (August) and a 3.5B 364-day Citi facility at SOFR+2.75-3.50% (October). The 20-F says the core business is not profitable and depends on raising equity or debt: dilution and refinancing are part of the base case, not a tail.

Minority stakes carried at 1,606.7M (ClickHouse 1,517.7M, Toloka preferred 86.5M) are separate, illiquid assets, not spendable cash; the H1 2026 net income of 430.8M is driven by a 780.6M ClickHouse revaluation gain, so reported net income is not a run rate.

The computed type (decline / turnaround) is an artefact of the Yandex-era companyfacts history (FY2024 -98.7%); the continuing business grew 4.5x in FY2025 and about 5.5x y/y in Q2 2026. Overridden to an early-scale hypergrowth infrastructure grower: the questions are delivery of contracted capacity, funding cost and dilution, pricing per MW, and returns on capital once depreciation matches revenue.

Only one quantified guide can be checked: year-end 2025 ARR 1.25B against a 0.9-1.1B guide (beat, n=1). FY2026 guidance (revenue 3.0-3.4B, ARR 7-9B, about 40% adjusted EBITDA margin, capex 20-25B, 800-1,000 MW connected) was issued in May and reaffirmed on 2026-08-12; it implies H2 revenue of 2.0-2.4B against H1 0.98B, and management says new capacity deals have no material effect on 2026 revenue. No FY2027 guidance yet (promised later in 2026). Q3 results come on 2026-11-12.

Q2 net loss -190.4M includes non-recurring Eigen AI acquisition charges (74.9M SBC and 41.0M post-combination compensation) and 36M deal/financing fees; normalized about -74.5M. Piotroski 6/7 and Altman Z'' 2.83 (safe) are computed on year-end 2025 and do not reflect the 2026 leverage build; Beneish unavailable; ROIC -8.7% (FY2025) and incremental ROIC -45% reflect capital not yet earning. The 20-F reports a material weakness (IT general controls, revenue recognition documentation).

Named competitors: CoreWeave (Q2 2026 revenue 2,575M, +112% y/y, operating margin -1.9%, RPO 103.7B; operating margin 16.9% in FY2024, its most mature year), Crusoe and Lambda (private), and the hyperscalers including Oracle. NBIS is about 23% of CoreWeave's size but growing faster. In October 2026 neocloud credit stress (CoreWeave bonds, a Gartner consolidation warning) and the hyperscaler capex read-through cut the share price about 26% in a month.

flags: Funding dependence: capex 20-25B in 2026 against negative free cash flow (about -3.6B in H1 even after 4.4B of prepayments); equity sales, pre-funded warrants and convertibles dilute holders; the 3.5B Citi facility matures in 364 days.
Customer concentration: three unnamed customers = 59% of Q2 2026 revenue; prepayments partly refundable; service credits and tranche termination rights on delivery delays.
Headline distortion: H1 2026 net income driven by a 780.6M ClickHouse revaluation gain; Q2 includes 115.9M of Eigen AI acquisition charges.
Depreciation policy change: server useful life extended from 4 to 5 years in 2026, lowering depreciation; GPU economic life under faster chip cycles is the counter-risk.
Material weakness in internal control (IT general controls, revenue recognition documentation) reported in the 20-F.
ROIC -8.7% (FY2025) and incremental ROIC -45%: returns on the build are not yet proven.
Forensic screens (Piotroski 6/7, Altman Z'' 2.83) are from year-end 2025, before debt rose to about 8.5B and capex to 8.1B in H1 2026: they overstate today's safety.
Execution: US site risk (Vineland NJ hearing adjourned, power moved to fuel cells); limited experience delivering multi-year hyperscaler contracts.
Geopolitical: Israel sites (4.3% of long-lived assets), export controls and a proposed BIS rule on IaaS customers, GPU supply concentrated in three suppliers.

economics.reason: Revenue is multi-year contracted capacity (RPO 37.5B, three-quarters beyond 12 months) with prepayments, and growth comes from capacity added, not from a price cycle; the cyclical-like risks (GPU-hour price declines as supply expands, AI-lab funding) are carried in the bear and the key risk, not by cycle normalization.

type.override_reason: Computed decline/turnaround reads the Yandex-era group revenue (FY2020-FY2023) and the 2024 divestiture as a collapse; the continuing AI cloud grew 4.5x in FY2025 and about 6x y/y in Q2 2026 with guided ARR 7-9B at end 2026. Valuation lens: scale-up FCFF with explicit reinvestment and financing, never a run-off DCF.

gaps: No revenue guidance track record (only one ARR guide checked); FY2027 guidance not issued yet.
Q3 2026 results (2026-11-12) are after as_of: the H2 ramp to the 3.0-3.4B guide is unverified.
Final terms of the August 2026 convertibles and post-June share count not read.
Price per GPU-hour, utilisation and capex per MW not disclosed: mature margin and sales-to-capital rest on segment EBITDA, landmark-deal pricing and CoreWeave's record.
Identities of the 24% / 21% / 14% customers not disclosed.
